logline: Three sex workers - Coral, Wendy, and Gina - flee their brutal pimp and his henchmen across Tenerife in a hyper-stylised, relentlessly propulsive chase series from the Money Heist creators.

bollymeter.basis: 92-percent Rotten Tomatoes from 13 critics - praise centred on kinetic energy, the lead trio's chemistry, and the show's unapologetic pulp register alongside serious trafficking themes.

pull_quotes.text: This isn't any kind of social-realist drama. It's pulp - very good pulp.
Wild cliffhanger endings should have you slamming 'next episode' faster.

seasons.review_body: Sky Rojo's first season landed in March 2021 trailing the enormous goodwill of Money Heist - and it largely justified the hype on its own pulp terms. Creator Alex Pina and Esther Martinez Lobato strip the narrative to its essentials: three women running, two men chasing, a Tenerife backdrop soaked in neon and club smoke. The 92-percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 13 critics reflected a genuine critical consensus that the show's velocity and tonal confidence were assets rather than evasions. TIME called it 'very good pulp', which is precisely the right frame: the series does not pretend to be a social-realist document about trafficking, but the horror underneath the stylised surface is always present. The lead trio - Veronika Sanchez, Lali Esposito, and Yany Prado - carry crackling chemistry through short, punchy episodes that rarely overstay their welcome.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The opener establishes the show's grammar in under 30 minutes: percussive editing, Tarantino-adjacent visual design, and three protagonists whose survival instincts override every other consideration. The inciting escape is both darkly funny and genuinely harrowing.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first chase sequence through Las Novias Club announces the show's visual register - and its willingness to be unsettling even while being stylish.

critic_note.text: A vivid, thundering denunciation of the sexual exploitation of women.

bollymeter.basis: 83-percent RT score but critically noted for losing momentum - subplots diluted Season 1's tight chase energy, and reviewers found the pacing inconsistent over the extended mid-section.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived four months after the first, with an 83-percent Rotten Tomatoes aggregate - technically positive but noted for a slackening of the relentless pace that gave Season 1 its identity. Additional subplots dilute the core fugitive-thriller structure; the show is at its best when Coral, Wendy, and Gina are sprinting, and Season 2 keeps slowing to manage threads that do not earn the screen time. Asier Etxeandia as Romeo remains the series' most compelling presence - morally repellent and somehow charismatic - and some of the standalone chase and confrontation sequences still land with Season 1's kinetic force. The season functions as connective tissue more than self-contained entertainment.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 loses the tight fugitive-thriller structure of Season 1 as additional plot lines dilute the core chase dynamic.

bollymeter.basis: 62-percent RT from a minimal sample; critics described it as 'a roller coaster' with an open resolution that divided audiences expecting a conclusive finale.

pull_quotes.text: A sort of roller coaster; we'll see if it ends on a high or a low.

seasons.review_body: The third and final season arrived in January 2023 with a 62-percent Rotten Tomatoes score from a thin critical sample - suggesting the show had settled into a niche rather than expanding it. Season 3 recovers some of the original's propulsion in individual sequences but ultimately ends the series in a way that left its most committed viewers debating whether the resolution honoured the premise. The series deserves credit for being genuinely about something - sexual exploitation, sisterhood, survival - even when its execution is uneven. Fans of Seasons 1 and 2 should watch to close the loop; casual viewers can safely treat Season 1 as a standalone.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 3 attempts a definitive conclusion to the three-season chase but delivers a mixed resolution that satisfied the core fanbase more than general audiences.
